title: An-Nasr: the help
hook: when help comes and people enter in crowds, praise and ask forgiveness (Surah 110)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Masad, and the uncle whose kinship didn't protect him. Your line was kin is not a guarantee. Did you catch yourself judging someone by who they belong to? Day one hundred sixty-four.

Think about the last time you won something. A game, an argument, a promotion, a parking spot. What did you do with the first ten seconds? A fist in the air, maybe. A text to someone who doubted you. It's the most natural thing in the world. Yesterday's surah was about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at the start, rejected by his own family on a hill in Mecca. Today's is about the end, when everything he'd hoped for came true. And what it tells him to do with the first ten seconds is not what you'd expect. Today: An-Nasr, the help.
screen: `THE FIRST TEN SECONDS OF WINNING.` → `FROM REJECTION TO VICTORY.` → `NOT WHAT YOU'D EXPECT.`

segments.voice: Surah one hundred ten, in Pickthall's translation: When Allah's succour and the triumph cometh And thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops, Then hymn the praises of thy Lord, and seek forgiveness of Him. Lo! He is ever ready to show mercy. Nasr means help, the kind that turns a struggle. Most commentators connect the surah with the opening of Mecca, around the year six hundred thirty, when the city that had driven the Prophet out opened to him, and people came to Islam in whole tribes at a time. Now look at the instruction. Not celebrate. Not remind them who was right. Praise your Lord, and ask forgiveness. Why forgiveness, at the moment of victory? Scholars give two answers. First, success is exactly when a person is most likely to forget where it came from, so you ask forgiveness for whatever pride slipped in. Second, a deeper reading. Bukhari records that Umar asked the senior companions what the surah meant, and most said it was a command to praise at victory. Then he asked the young Ibn Abbas, who said: it's the sign that the Prophet's time is near. His work is finished. Umar said: I know nothing of it except what you know. The Prophet died about two years after the opening of Mecca. Aisha reports that after this surah came, he would often say in his bowing and prostration: glory be to You, our Lord, and praise; O Allah, forgive me. And the sirah describes him entering Mecca with his head bowed so low it nearly touched his saddle. Win humbly.
screen: `NASR — THE HELP THAT TURNS IT.` · `THE OPENING OF MECCA.` · `PRAISE, AND ASK FORGIVENESS.` · `THE SIGN THAT HIS TIME WAS NEAR.` · then, large: `WIN HUMBLY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Sit, and bring back a recent success, even a small one. Something that went right, that you're a little proud of. Feel it. Now notice who and what helped: people, timing, things you didn't control. If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah, I seek Allah's forgiveness, for any pride that slipped in. If you don't, simply let a little of the credit go back to where it came from. The bell holds the time.
An-Nasr. The help, the name of Surah one hundred ten: when help and victory come, praise your Lord and ask forgiveness. Today's word.
Your line: win humbly. The next time something goes your way today, spend the first ten seconds on thanks, not on proving anyone wrong. Day one hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: Many Muslims say astaghfirullah and subhan Allah after a success, following this surah; the Prophet's words in bowing and prostration after it was revealed are still said by many in their prayers.
